# Voynich manuscript: strategies log

One row per strategy: method and control, result, verdict. Earlier work is summarised in FINDINGS.md.

| ID | Method and control | Result | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| v8:V-1.1 | Positive/negative calibration of spectral seriation: Isidore Etymologiae (Latin) cut into pages with the exact Voynich page/line lengths (225 pages); plain, with a slowly drifting homophonic letter cipher (23 letters switch variant at random times, logistic width 0.08), and with tokens redealt across pages. Stats: split-half |rho| (even vs odd lines seriated separately) and |rho| of recovered order vs true order | plain: split 0.46, ~truth 0.34 (TSP 0.33); drift cipher: split 0.94, ~truth 0.98 (TSP 0.69); redeal: split 0.02 / 0.07 | Method calibrated: a drifting key is recovered as a 1-D order; redeal kills it |
| v8:V-1.2 | Same seriation on Voynich (ZL3b, P/C/R lines, pages >= 30 tokens, words with ? dropped); null = tokens redealt; TSP path gain vs redeal null; recovered order vs binding order | split 0.88 (redeal 0.01); TSP gain 0.058 (Latin plain 0.035, cipher 0.154); Fiedler~binding |rho| 0.66; Fiedler~Currier B 0.80 | A strong, reproducible 1-D axis exists (split-half 0.88 vs 0.01 null; Latin+drifting key 0.94, plain Latin 0.46). At whole-book level it is mainly the A/B axis (0.80) plus section; it matches binding only through A/B (0.66) |
| v8:V-1.3 | Drift inside homogeneous strata (language x illustration): split-half |rho| vs within-stratum token redeal (10 seeds); matched Latin plain and drift-cipher blocks of the same size and line template | Currier A (all) n=114 split 0.66 (null 0.07, z 7.3) ~binding 0.59; Currier B (all) n=82 split 0.82 (null 0.09, z 11.8) ~binding 0.29; A herbal n=95 split 0.19 (null 0.09, z 1.3) ~binding 0.33; B herbal n=32 split 0.71 (null 0.17, z 4.7) ~binding 0.43; B bio (Q M) n=20 split 0.77 (null 0.13, z 8.3) ~binding 0.09; B stars (illus S, lang B) n=23 split 0.91 (null 0.10, z 10.7) ~binding 0.06; pharma (illus P) n=16 split 0.16 (null 0.17, z -0.1) ~binding 0.38 || controls: Currier A (all): Latin plain 0.26 (z 2.5), cipher 0.76 (z 13.3, ~truth 0.95); Currier B (all): Latin plain 0.40 (z 6.2), cipher 0.08 (z -0.7, ~truth 0.84); A herbal: Latin plain 0.07 (z 0.2), cipher 0.84 (z 12.4, ~truth 0.95); B herbal: Latin plain 0.74 (z 3.0), cipher 0.31 (z 0.4, ~truth 0.61); B bio (Q M): Latin plain 0.51 (z 7.8), cipher 0.46 (z 0.6, ~truth 0.39); B stars (illus S, lang B): Latin plain 0.84 (z 8.5), cipher 0.57 (z 1.8, ~truth 0.61); pharma (illus P): Latin plain 0.19 (z -0.6), cipher 0.69 (z 7.4, ~truth 0.21) | Split verdict. (a) Currier A herbal (95 pages, all hand 1): NO recoverable clock (split 0.19, z 1.3); a drifting key of the control strength in a block of the same size is recovered at 0.84 split / 0.95 truth, so A herbal pages are exchangeable: no writing order is recoverable there. (b) B strata (bio, stars, B herbal) show strong 1-D axes (0.71-0.91), but plain Latin topic continuity gives the same values (0.51-0.84) at these small n, so these axes are not yet shown to be time rather than topic/hand. (c) Pharma flat. Whole-A axis (0.66) is section, not time |
| v8:V-1.4 | Quire contiguity along the whole-book seriation: mean |rank gap| of same-quire page pairs vs quire labels permuted (300x), all pages and within A / within B | all: 38.0 vs 75.4 (z -24.7); within A: 25.9 vs 39.8 (z -12.4); within B: 20.8 vs 31.4 (z -8.2) | Quires are very compact in vocabulary space, also inside each language (z -12, -8). Control: hand labels, binding order | B herbal axis runs hand 3 (f94-95) / hand 2 -> hand 5 (f41, f48, f57) at the far end; B stars (all hand 3) and bio (all hand 2): recto and verso of the same leaf come out within 2 ranks in 8/11 stars leaves (5 directly adjacent) and 6/10 bio leaves (3 adjacent); order vs binding |rho| 0.06-0.09 | Within-B axes partly = scribe (B herbal). The leaf (r+v) behaves as a unit; quantified with a proper null in cycle 3 (V-3.x). Binding order inside stars/bio carries no vocabulary sequence |
| v8:V-2.1 | Graded-position test. Page B-score = mean token LLR (B vs A unigram, leave-one-page-out), from even lines and from odd lines separately; Spearman of the two inside each language after demeaning by section x hand. Null: tokens redealt within language x section x hand (10x). Controls: Isidore pages, same templates and group sizes, (G) one key drifting through the whole book, (D) two fixed keys with an abrupt switch | Voynich within A rho 0.52 (null -0.04, z 6.3); within B 0.51 (null 0.03, z 4.6). Control G (drift): A 0.39, B 0.54. Control D (discrete): A 0.21, B 0.51 | Not discriminating. Pages do hold a stable individual position on the A-B scale inside each language (z 6.3, 4.6 vs redeal), but the two-fixed-keys control (no drift at all) gives 0.21/0.51 from topic leakage alone, and the drifting-key control 0.39/0.54. Voynich A (0.52) exceeds both; B does not. A stable within-A position is real but cannot be credited to time rather than subject |
| v8:V-2.2 | Gap test: share of pages whose whole-page B-score lies in the middle third between the A and B medians. Controls G and D as above | Voynich 0.036 (7 pages); G 0.122; D 0.000 | Mostly a jump. Only 7/196 pages (3.6%) sit in the middle third; a drifting key gives 12%, two fixed keys 0%. The 7 intermediates are not scattered: 4 A pharma pages (f88v, f89r1, f89r2, f102v2), hand-3 A page f58r, hand-5 B page f57r, one A herbal (f90v1). Group medians order as A herbal (-0.96) < A pharma (-0.50) < hand-3 A (+0.08) < hand-5 B herbal (+0.48) < hand-2/3 B herbal and stars (+0.72..0.82) < hand-2 bio (+1.53). So the A->B scale is a ladder of section x hand groups with few in-between pages, not a smooth page-by-page drift (the gradual-section ordering itself is Timm 2014; the calibration against keyed controls is new) |
| v8:V-2.3 | Oddities as stages: inside A and inside B (demeaned by section x hand), Spearman of page B-score computed WITHOUT the feature-carrying words vs the feature. Calibration: same logic on controls with feature = share of tokens carrying a variant letter (letter excluded from score) | m/g line-end quota (B-A +0.074): A rho +0.15 p=0.11, B rho +0.02 p=0.88; q-initial share (B-A +0.060): A rho +0.02 p=0.85, B rho +0.19 p=0.084; ed share (B-A +0.197): A rho +0.11 p=0.26, B rho -0.37 p=0.00073; -ol/-or share (B-A -0.134): A rho -0.14 p=0.12, B rho -0.11 p=0.35; mean line length (B-A +2.010): A rho +0.16 p=0.097, B rho -0.04 p=0.7 || control G (drift) median rho A 0.30 / B 0.09; control D (discrete) median rho A nan / B -0.04 | Oddities are NOT stages along the A-B scale. Within A, none of m/g quota, q share, ed share, -ol/-or share or line length follows residual B-ness (all p > 0.09; drifting-key control gives median rho 0.30). Within B the strongest effect has the WRONG sign: pages richer in ed have less B-like other vocabulary (rho -0.37, p = 0.0007), transcription-robust in IT2a (-0.34, p = 0.002) and unchanged when all e-words are removed from the score (-0.39). B-ness is at least two-dimensional inside B (an ed-load axis trading off against other B-markers), so A/B cannot be one drifting scalar |
| v8:V-2.4 | Transcription robustness of V-2.3 (tools/v8_cycle2b.py): IT2a; score excluding ed-words vs excluding every e-containing word | ZL within B -0.37 / -0.39; IT within B -0.34 / -0.34; within A +0.09..+0.13 (n.s.) in both | Transcription-robust (Wells/IM77-style caveat: ZL and IT read the same pages). | v8:V-3.1 | Physical writing unit. Residual page similarity (Hellinger, double-centred within language x hand x illustration) for pair classes inside a quire: LEAF (r+v of one leaf), SIDE (conjugate leaves, same face of the unfolded sheet), CROSS (conjugate, opposite faces), OPEN (facing pages in current binding), OTHER. Null: page identities permuted within quire x group (2000x). Controls: Isidore poured into the same layout in book order, and in sheet-face order | Voynich ZL: LEAF +0.037 (n=117, z +4.3, p=0), SIDE +0.038 (n=110, z +4.2, p=0), CROSS +0.029 (n=109, z +2.4, p=0.008), OPEN +0.009 (n=44, z +0.0, p=0.478), OTHER -0.001 (n=721, z -9.2, p=1), SIDE-CROSS +0.009 (n=0, z +1.1, p=0.133), LEAF-SIDE -0.001 (n=0, z -0.1, p=0.548) | A herbal: LEAF +0.061 (n=49, z +4.6, p=0), SIDE +0.049 (n=47, z +3.4, p=0), CROSS +0.042 (n=47, z +2.3, p=0.0115), OPEN +0.020 (n=23, z +0.5, p=0.309), OTHER +0.003 (n=357, z -6.8, p=1), SIDE-CROSS +0.007 (n=0, z +0.6, p=0.26), LEAF-SIDE +0.012 (n=0, z +0.9, p=0.173) | B: LEAF +0.039 (n=36, z +3.5, p=0), SIDE +0.031 (n=38, z +2.3, p=0.012), CROSS +0.035 (n=35, z +2.8, p=0.0035), OPEN -0.000 (n=18, z -0.1, p=0.543), OTHER -0.006 (n=343, z -6.3, p=1), SIDE-CROSS -0.004 (n=0, z -0.4, p=0.667), LEAF-SIDE +0.008 (n=0, z +0.9, p=0.186) | IT2a: LEAF +0.034 (n=117, z +3.3, p=0.001), SIDE +0.043 (n=110, z +5.0, p=0), CROSS +0.027 (n=109, z +1.7, p=0.04), OPEN +0.010 (n=44, z +0.1, p=0.485), OTHER -0.000 (n=721, z -8.8, p=1), SIDE-CROSS +0.016 (n=0, z +2.1, p=0.02), LEAF-SIDE -0.009 (n=0, z -1.3, p=0.895) || control book order: LEAF +0.064 (n=117, z +7.9, p=0), SIDE +0.012 (n=110, z -2.2, p=0.986), CROSS +0.009 (n=109, z -2.5, p=0.996), OPEN +0.078 (n=44, z +6.7, p=0), OTHER +0.010 (n=721, z -6.8, p=1), SIDE-CROSS +0.002 (n=0, z +0.2, p=0.44), LEAF-SIDE +0.052 (n=0, z +6.3, p=0) | control sheet-face order: LEAF +0.034 (n=117, z +2.1, p=0.0215), SIDE +0.062 (n=110, z +6.9, p=0), CROSS +0.038 (n=109, z +2.3, p=0.0155), OPEN +0.040 (n=44, z +2.1, p=0.025), OTHER +0.008 (n=721, z -10.8, p=1), SIDE-CROSS +0.024 (n=0, z +3.0, p=0.0025), LEAF-SIDE -0.027 (n=0, z -3.2, p=1) | The writing unit is the BIFOLIO, not the book page sequence. Conjugate leaves are as alike as the two sides of one leaf (ZL: SIDE z +4.2, CROSS +2.4, LEAF +4.3), while facing pages of the current binding are at chance (OPEN z 0.0). Book-order writing (control) gives the reverse: LEAF/OPEN high, conjugates below chance. Same in A herbal, in B, and in IT2a. Face of the sheet (SIDE minus CROSS) is not established: ZL z +1.1, IT z +2.1, A herbal +0.6, B -0.4. NOT NEW in substance: Layfield & Davis 2026 (LSA, singulion hypothesis) report elevated within-bifolio similarity and text written before binding; this is an independent, control-calibrated replication with hand/language/section removed |
| v8:V-3.2 | Jumps along the current binding order: boundary score = residual similarity of the 2 pages before vs the 2 after (whole book, double-centred). Boundary types: quire edge, hand change, language change, section change, bifolio change in a quire with nothing else changing, and leaf change inside one bifolio. Calibration: partial key change (3 letters get a variant) planted at a random point in Isidore pages (30 trials) | mean score / share in sharpest 10%%: quire n=19 +0.041 / 0.21; hand n=33 -0.013 / 0.64; lang n=31 -0.023 / 0.68; section n=27 +0.056 / 0.07; bifolio n=68 +0.075 / 0.25; same-leaf n=123 +0.089 / 0.02; clean bifolio change n=44 +0.123 vs same-bifolio leaf change n=14 +0.131 (MW p=0.35); sharpest homogeneous jumps: f48r|f48v -0.015, f41r|f41v -0.011, f44r|f44v -0.009, f54r|f54v -0.004, f49r|f49v -0.001, f30r|f30v +0.001, f93r|f93v +0.005, f42r|f42v +0.008 || planted key change: median rank quantile 0.000, in lowest 5% in 90% of trials | Jumps sit at hand and language changes (64-68% of them in the sharpest 10% of boundaries), not at quire edges (21%) or section changes (7%); same-leaf boundaries almost never (2%). A 3-letter key change is caught 90% of the time, so a key change of that size inside a run would have been seen. (The list of homogeneous jumps here is contaminated by windows that cross hands; superseded by V-3.4) |
| v8:V-3.3 | Blind conjugate identification (prediction test): recto+verso merged into leaves; within quire x language x hand x illustration, is each leaf's most similar leaf (double-centred Hellinger) its conjugate? Chance = sum of 1/(k-1). Controls: Isidore poured in book order and in sheet-face order | ZL: 28/66 hits vs 12.9 expected (z +4.7); IT2a: 28/66 vs 12.9 (z +4.7); control book order 10/66 vs 12.9 (z -0.9); control sheet-face 51/66 vs 12.9 (z +11.8) | Prediction passes: from vocabulary alone, a leaf's nearest leaf is its physical conjugate 28/66 times against 12.9 expected (z +4.7, same in IT2a; transcription-robust, not replicated). Book-order control is at chance (10/66), sheet-wise control far above (51/66). The Voynich sits between: bifolios carry a shared vocabulary state, but weaker than a strict sheet-by-sheet text flow |
| v8:V-3.4 | Jumps inside homogeneous runs: boundaries in binding order whose 2+2-page window lies in one quire x language x hand x illustration group; boundary score as V-3.2. Calibration: a 3-letter partial key change planted at one such position in Isidore pages with the same layout (30 trials) | 106 homogeneous boundaries; sharpest 5%: f5r|f5v +0.020 (same leaf), f5v|f6r +0.018 (bifolio change), f6v|f7r +0.009 (bifolio change), f23v|f24r +0.033 (bifolio change), f52v|f53r +0.037 (same bifolio), f53v|f54r +0.018 (bifolio change); mean score same-leaf +0.130 (n=52) vs leaf change +0.124 (n=54) || planted key change: median quantile 0.000, in lowest 5% in 90% of trials | No hidden key change inside homogeneous runs. The 6 sharpest homogeneous boundaries (out of 106) are small and 5/6 fall at bifolio changes (f5v|f6r, f6v|f7r, f23v|f24r, f53v|f54r) or inside central bifolios (f5r|f5v, f52v|f53r) - i.e. the steps between writing units, not breaks of a cipher. A planted 3-letter key change would rank in the lowest 5% in 90% of trials |

| v15:V-15.final | Word lengths (glyph units, EVA characters, pen strokes), uncertain-space gaps, words per line, line totals and length differences as the carrier of a hidden letter stream. (1) Structure: repeats, neighbour MI across and within lines, entropy rate, periodicity, 'is length a privileged vocabulary partition', against word shuffles within line / page / section and a position-preserving null. (2) Search: ~6,700 solver runs, ~10 M random codebooks scored, ~16,600 annealing chains; 7 letter models (Latin, Italian, German, Old Czech, Hebrew, Occitan, Greek); 8 schemes (len, pair, bacon2, baconT, tri3, mod4pair, line total mod 20-30, delta mod 6-10); held-out halves; the same search on shuffled-length nulls. (3) Controls: Caesar planted in the lengths (5 codes) and natural Latin and Italian lengths | (1) No excess structure: no excess repeated length runs (z <= 1.4; planted z 82-410), no length link across the line break (z -1.1; planted z +56), and length is no more structured than the first glyph (0.015 vs 0.018; in planted texts the first glyph carries ~0). (2) Best Voynich decode +0.03 bits/letter over the best null, never readable; planted Caesar +0.3 to +1.3 (readable when the code is lossless); natural prose lengths +0.1 to +0.4. (3) Side results: uncertain spaces bunch toward line ends (crowding); a period-8 rhythm in lengths is line layout | Grade A (negative): the Voynich length channels carry no hidden letter stream of these kinds, in any of the seven languages, at a size where a planted one is recovered with a 10-40x margin. Upper bound: a lossless code in >= half the words would give ~1 bit/letter, a lossy one-letter-per-length code ~0.3; observed 0.03. Lengths behave as a by-product of the words (the junction coupling), not as a separate channel. Methodological caveat (new): a homophonic key bends any language model onto a structured stream, so the planted Latin also 'decodes' as German, Czech or Greek at nearly the same margin. Such searches detect 'message-like', not 'which language', and must be calibrated on natural-language length streams, which themselves beat their shuffles at z up to 23. Grade C: would support 'mechanism' if, in a correction set drawn from the images, corrected Voynich words stay far rarer than Latin's at the same corpus size; would kill if the gap closes |

NEW copied-generator control (exemplar restored after neighbour-glyph slips): word ratio 1.19, same sign as Latin | Planted rule repair vs word repair: separated. | v24:V-24.F3 | What do the Voynich corrections enforce? | n 4: no rule beyond the null family-wise (zmax 3.9, FW p 0.58). Before-forms 3/4 words (random edits 0.25, tail p 0.027), 4/4 legal: Latin- or copy-like, but ordinary ZL ambiguity pairs give >= 3/4 word pairs in 45% of 4-subsets | Nothing established. | v24:V-24.F4 | Power | Latin-like vs copy-like at 95% needs ~32-48 genuine before/after pairs; copy vs rule-repair ~32 | Prediction: >= 50 erasure/overwrite pairs read from the vellum would decide it; transcriber variants cannot (they look Latin-like by construction: word ratio 2.53) |
| v24:V-24.F5 | After-only lead | 20 ZL-noted corrected words: only 10/20 occur elsewhere vs 0.79 for same-length tokens (p 0.001); Latin corrected words also rarer than average (0.90 vs 0.99) | Grade C: corrections fall on rare words in both scripts; transcriber selection is the simplest cause |
| v24:V-24.F | Overall | - | THE CORRECTIONS ARE TOO FEW TO BE A RULEBOOK. The method separates planted rule repair from planted word repair, and shows that real Latin corrections are neither (legal slips into other real words). A copied meaningless generator shares that sign, so meaning vs mechanism needs ~50 genuine Voynich corrections; transcriptions give 4, and ink anomalies on 25 pages do not find the known ones. Negative/inconclusive. Grade A for the census (24 marked, 4 usable); C for every Voynich lean |

### v21: forge the Voynich, then catch the forgery (4 Oct 2026; `loops/v21_final.txt`)
Twelve forgers (junction resyntheses, slot generator, page topic, kitchen sink, line-width filling, a GRU language model, copy-and-vary, survivor-targeted) against ~52,000 page discriminators (ridge on random 6-feature subsets, full ridge, boosting) and CNN line/paragraph models, cross-validated by page. Controls: forgery vs forgery, forger output re-forged by itself, a planted long-range re-use, and Latin and Italian herbals forged the same way.

| Run | Method and control | Result | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| v21:V-21.1 | Forger ladder F0-F7 vs 79 page features, 5 seeds; null, negative, planted, Latin/Italian herbal controls | Every forger caught: F3 junction resynthesis 0.933, F7 kitchen sink + width 0.957 (null 0.50, negative 0.59, planted 0.70; Latin 0.92, Italian 0.92) | No forger passes. Herbals are caught by topic re-use, the Voynich by local self-similarity and in-page drift |
| v21:V-21.2 | GRU forger (F8) and CNN line/paragraph discriminators | GRU caught at 0.997 (invents non-words). CNN: F3 0.54-0.59, null 0.50, but planted long-range re-use missed (0.50) | Learned local models are blind beyond ~9 units; not used for verdicts |
| v21:V-21.3 | Copy-and-vary forgers F9/F10 (rich junction key, Timm-Schinner self-citation with real edit operations, paragraph topic), ZL3b and IT2a | F10 0.934 / 0.928 (negative floor 0.66); herbals 0.90/0.84 (floor 0.64). Voynich survivors: para_first_in_rest -6.8, vert_last +6.2, mg_line_var -5.4, first_eq_lag1 +5.2 | Margin over floor equals the herbals', on a different axis: layout-local, never topical |
| v21:V-21.4 | F11 adds one mechanism per survivor; fresh seeds | Targeted survivors closed, AUC unchanged (0.926); near_far (+8 to +9) and ch/sh runs (-4.6) surface; herbals still caught by topic (0.93/0.90). vert_last is not vertical (same at column offsets, z 6.4 vs page line-shuffle) | Whack-a-mole. Generator-like in kind, beyond every single known generator. Grade B |
| v21:V-21.1.1 | Ladder on Voynich: F0 section x position unigram; F1 whole-book junction (v17 rule); F2 F1 + position tables; F3 junction per section + position (v17 resynthesis); F4 slot generator (in-word unit trigram per section x position class); F5 F3 + page topic (lam 0.3: draw from the page's own successor table); F6 F5 + line-initial chain + reduplication + self-citation, (lam, cite, redup) grid-calibrated to the real repeat-by-distance profile (V: 0.35, 0.01, 0); F7 F6 filling each line to the real line's width instead of its word count | Page AUC (ridge / boosting, mean of 5 seeds): F0 0.946/0.955; F1 0.999/0.998; F2 0.999/0.999; F3 0.933/0.950; F4 0.998/0.993; F5 0.952/0.940; F6 0.952/0.946; F7 0.957/0.945. Random 6-feature subsets beating the null's 99th percentile (0.597): 78-98% | Every forger is caught at AUC >= 0.93. Section tables matter most (F1/F2 -> F3: 0.999 -> 0.933); the slot generator is the worst forger (0.998). Page topic, chain, reduplication, self-citation and line-width filling do not bring the Voynich closer (0.95) |
| v21:V-21.1.2 | NULL: forgery vs forgery (two seeds of the same forger as 'real' and 'forged'), F3 and F7, all corpora | V F7 0.500/0.485, V F3 0.486/0.522, LA 0.530/0.507, IT 0.484/0.502; subset AUC max 0.58-0.63, 0-4% above null 99th | Clean: the discriminators find nothing in forgery vs forgery |

A residual 0.54-0.59 comes from F7's token-count drift and from vocabulary shrinkage on resampling; it sets the floor any 'surviving' signal must clear |

Surviving features vs F7 (all 5 seeds |z|>=4, controls |z|<3.5): LA para_first_in_rest +8.1, ttr -7.3, rep_any +7.3, rep_line2_4 +7.1, rep_adj -6.7, near_far +6.2, rep_prevline +5.5; IT wlen_ac2 +9.2, rep_any +8.5, ttr -8.5, rep_sameline +7.4, rep_line2_4 +7.3, rep_adj -6.3 | Passes: real herbals are caught through meaning-level features (topic words named in a paragraph's first line and re-used 2-4 lines later, low TTR, no adjacent repeats) |

Its paragraph-first line is LESS re-used later (z -7), where the herbals re-use it MORE (+8). Grade B: the Voynich has structure beyond every forger here, of a copy-and-vary kind, not of a topic kind |

### v27: the lines were cards, and the deck was shuffled (4 Oct 2026; `loops/v27_final.txt`)
Every body line is a card; the best order is searched (exact DP / simulated annealing in C) within paragraphs and across the whole book, under a junction scorer trained only on within-line word pairs plus a lexical scorer, without ever seeing the written order. Controls: Latin and Italian herbals (positive), cross-page independent lines (negative), word-shuffled and Markov-resynthesised nulls, planted hidden continuity (also across pages), a two-witness test with ~2,000 random junction hypotheses.

| v41:V-41.2.V | Cycle verdict | In all 9 groups x 2 transliterations the 11 traits co-move along the A->B direction inside one hand (S z +4.0 to +10.7 except hand-2 bio z 1.7-1.8 and small pharma z 2.6-2.7). The A->B orientation is special: random sign patterns are as coherent in <= 0.7% of draws for 13 of 18 runs. S/R 0.12-0.43, at or above real dated German across texts (0.08-0.18), while the German within-one-manuscript floor is 0. The held-out order beats the shuffled-trait null only modestly (z +1.0 to +2.9). Word-initial benched gallows, the class feature of v36, does NOT take part (-0.43 to +0.40, sign unstable): bench loss is a between-group jump, endings and e-load drift within hands | Grade B: every hand carries a one-dimensional, transcription-robust A->B axis of spelling habits from page to page (a within-hand version of the A/B ladder). Whether that axis is time or subject is not settled here; cycle 3 checks it against the physical book |

| v41:V-41.3.V | Cycle verdict | Two different behaviours. In B (hands 2 and 3, both transliterations) the clock is shared by the two sides of a leaf and by conjugate leaves (B_all leaf z -3.2/-3.4, conjugates -2.6/-2.4; hand-2 bio conjugates -3.0/-3.1; hand-3 stars leaf -2.5/-2.5): a bifolio is one moment of the drift, as a writing-batch clock predicts. In hand-1 A there is no bifolio clustering (z -0.1 to +1.6), but the clock rises with foliation (herbal rho +0.33 ZL / +0.31 IT). Hand 2: inner bifolios less B-like than outer (depth rho -0.32/-0.34; bio -0.55/-0.61, few bifolios) and the second leaf of a pair less B-like in 73% of 48 pairs | Grade B: in B the drift clock is a bifolio property (fits the v8 bifolio writing unit, now for spelling habits not just vocabulary). Grade C: the hand-1 clock runs along the binding order (cycle 4 tests it); would support: the rise holds within quires and only for the A->B orientation; would kill: carried only by between-quire differences or by any random trait combination |

With the data-driven merges the Voynich moves, if anywhere, TOWARD the generator class, while every planted language moves back to language by the same procedure. The twin structure is real (planted-band I) but its collapse does not uncover a language-like text. Grade A (negative), held out and in two transcriptions |

| v42:V-42.1.V | Cycle verdict | (1) The v31 'generator' label is not specific to mechanical generators: in the clean world 65% (collapsed) / 61% (bigram scheme) of 31 surviving random classifiers call the CS a GENERATOR (Voynich 87%), while the raw stroke scheme reads as GIBBERISH (45%) / GEN (32%). Single-model posteriors depend on the unit scheme (raw -> GIBB 0.70; col -> LANG 0.68; sb -> GEN 0.48). (2) At the CS's own OCR noise (n18 world) the classifiers weaken (LOCO 0.68, 6 survivors) and neither CS nor Voynich GEN posterior beats the label-permutation null (p 0.32 / 0.17). (3) Hub test: the CS is nearer the Voynich than any of 123 training texts, though the Voynich attracts no training corpus | Grade B: a long meaningless book by one hand lands in the 'generator' region the Voynich occupies, so v31's GEN verdict cannot separate 'mechanical generator' from 'long asemic writing'. Grade C: the Voynich's nearest real neighbour is the Codex Seraphinianus; would support: a second, independent long asemic book (hand-transcribed) also lands next to it; would kill: an independent long asemic transcription that lands with short gibberish or languages |

| v42:V-42.2.V | Cycle verdict | (1) Per metric the Voynich leaves the language range on 7-9 of 13-15 LONG metrics; the CS leaves it on the same side on 6-8 of them (no lexical gaps / gap ratio V 1.05, CS 0.92-0.98, languages 0.81; low h2 and h3 ratios; strong in-word slot order and position-MI; glyph arrow V 2.41 = CS 2.42, languages 1.86, generators 2.23; line-initial and line-final effects). Over 50-100 corpora only Chinese Pinyin ties the CS for the most shared departures (line metrics dropped). The CS is the nearest group median on 7 of 15 metrics in both worlds. (2) With a 6th class ASEMIC trained only on CS volumes 1 and 2 (held-out volume recognised 2/2 in every run), the Voynich is absorbed at the 3000-token scale: ASEMIC 0.93-0.98 with line metrics, 0.64-0.80 without, A and B both; 0 of 44-91 held-out training corpora and 0 of 3 never-trained odd texts (Martian glossolalia, Lingua Ignota, Steganographia; ASEMIC <= 0.01) are absorbed. At 250 tokens it is a three-way split (ASEMIC 0.26-0.74, GEN, GIBB). (3) Weakness: battery-level LOCO among the four or five base classes is poor (0.29-0.45), so the base classes are not well separated by these 13-15 metrics; the ASEMIC result rests on the CS being a tight, distinct class | Grade B: on the classic battery the Voynich's profile is that of the one long asemic book available, more than of any generator, cipher, language or short gibberish; this holds without line metrics and in noise-matched form. Grade C: 'the Voynich is a long asemic book' as a class claim (n = 1 reference book, machine-read at 18% error); would support: another long one-hand asemic text joins the class; would kill: a mechanical generator or a long meaningful text in a minim script (stroke transliteration) is absorbed by ASEMIC as well |

| v42:V-42.3.V | Cycle verdict | Calibration first: the planted hardening (0 -> 40% slot-generator words along Isidore) is caught by the GEN-posterior trend (rho +0.23, p 0.001) and rigidity (+0.20) but NOT by the 6-trait index (-0.02; planted generator words raise TTR and lower position-MI), so only the GEN trend is a calibrated hardening detector. Its false-positive rate is not small: 1 of 6 long language corpora (German Lite, a multi-work compilation) gives GEN rho +0.18 (p 0.002), and single traits drift in 4 of 6 languages (rigidity -0.27 to -0.33) -> treat |rho| < 0.3 as noise. Result: the Codex Seraphinianus does NOT drift toward generator statistics; it drifts AWAY (GEN rho -0.31, p < 0.001 over 442 windows; volume 1 GEN 0.34 -> volume 2 0.18; no trend inside either volume, -0.01 / -0.08). The Voynich shows no GEN trend in folio order (n18 -0.06, clean 0.00; Currier A -0.09, B 0.00, hand 1 -0.09) and B is no more generator-like than A (0.34 -> 0.31 n18; 0.27 -> 0.18 clean). Short gibberish writers do not harden from their first to their last 100 tokens (GEN up in 20/30, Wilcoxon p 0.40; the language control shows a comparable shift, p 0.003, so this paired test is uncalibrated) | Grade B (negative): the 'habits harden into a system' hypothesis is killed for the one long asemic book measured -- Serafini's text is generator-like from its first pages and becomes less so; the Voynich likewise has no hardening trend. Grade C parallel: in both books the second 'dialect' (CS volume 2, Currier B) is the less generator-like one; would support: the same A->B direction in another long asemic text; would kill: the CS V1/V2 difference reverses under a hand transcription (OCR artefact) |

Grade C: Serafini re-used invented 'names' within a page, the Voynich scribe did not; would support: a hand transcription of CS caption pages shows the same rare-word bursts; would kill: the bursts come from OCR duplicates (repeated word images) |

| v45:V-45.F | THE RESIDUAL IS THE MESSAGE (6 cycles; tools/v45_*.py; loops/v45_cycle1-6.txt, v45_final.txt): v26 rule model cross-fitted; residual = which allowed alternative was chosen, per word and per page (observed minus rule-expected). Controls: rule-only generators, a richer misfit generator, Latin and Gerard text pushed through planted verbose codes in the same rules | Excess surprise V +0.19 bits/word = misfit generator +0.24 (codes +0.44 to +1.26); residual repeats within bifolio/quire (z 7-10, both transcriptions; generators 0); no drawing tracking (residual below surface, random search held-out z -1.4; plant discovery +3.8); residual stream not language-like; PIT surplus = opening lines (42% off-table words vs 26%) | Grade B: residual = misfit plus writing-unit drift, not a message; Grade C: openings hold entry-specific content. Blind to proportional (steganographic) or letter-level codes. Not cracked |
| v45:V-45.1.0 | RULE MODEL. v26 minimal genome (rich junction key, line-initial chain, paragraph drift; section x position tables) plus backoff to the last-unit junction table and section unigram (weights 0.3/0.3/0.4 tuned on V cross-fit), slot-template escape for words outside the fitting half. 2-fold cross-fit by pages: fitted on one half, every word of the other half scored. Per word: surprisal, model entropy, rank and PIT of the chosen word among the allowed alternatives; per page: expected count of every type (residual usage = (observed - expected)/sqrt(expected)) | V ZL 11.44 bits/word (unsmoothed genome 12.26); 30% of tokens lie outside every table (fold-new or table-absent words) | Rule model built; identical pipeline for every corpus |
| v45:V-45.1.1 | CORPORA through the same pipeline. Negatives: GEN0, GEN1 = the v26 minimal genome's own output on the V skeleton (rules, no message); PL = the richer v26 planted genome (copy-and-vary, ch/sh runs, m/g quota: rules the rule model lacks, so misfit without message). Positives: Latin Isidore XVI-XVII pushed through a planted verbose encoding with the same Voynich-fitted rules: LAw one Voynich word per Latin word (Latin types dealt into 400 buckets of Voynich types), LAl one word per Latin letter (26 buckets); the rule model picks the word inside the bucket. Gerard Herball page text the same way (GEw, GEl) | 202 V pages / 34,684 words; IT2a 201 / 34,235; GEN 34.5k; PL 34.7k; LAw 98 pages / 19.2k; LAl 66.6k; GEw 144 pages; GEl 144 pages | - |
| v45:V-45.1.2 | HOW HARD ARE THE CHOICES PUSHED? Excess surprise = surprisal minus model entropy at that slot (bits/word, in-table words); PIT histogram (10 bins) and KS distance from uniform | V +0.19 (KS 0.056; PIT bins rise to 0.142 at 0.8-0.9); IT2a +0.21 (0.054); GEN0/GEN1 -0.38/-0.39 (0.081/0.086); PL (misfit, no message) +0.24 (0.034); LAl (letter code) +0.44 (0.066); LAw (word code) +1.26 (0.210, PIT piles at the improbable end) | The Voynich deviates from its rules exactly as much as a richer generator with no message deviates from a poorer model (+0.19 vs +0.24); a crude bucket code pushes 2-6x harder. Upper bound: any message carried by crude forcing of choices costs <= ~0.2 bits/word of excess; a code that picks in proportion to the rule probabilities (perfect steganography) is invisible to this measure |
| v45:V-45.1.3 | DOES THE RESIDUAL REPEAT WITH SHARED LABELS? Mean cosine of residual usage for page pairs sharing a label minus pairs not sharing it, within section (section: across all; illustration type: within Currier language); null = labels permuted within stratum (1000x). Compared with raw tf-idf. V and IT2a; GEN0/GEN1/PL negatives | V raw: section z +10.9, hand +4.1, quire +10.3, bifolio +12.8. V residual: section -15.6 (removed; same in every corpus, -15 to -22: subtracting a section model), hand +2.0, quire +7.4, bifolio +9.6, illus -11.2. Surface layer = ch~sh, k~t, p~f by run habit and line position; benched gallows = ch + gallows; e-padding; optional q- after -y (edge pairing); line machinery; lines sealed. Extraction frozen on the discovery half (E1c: drop q-, sh=ch, bench = ch + gallows, k=t, p=f, delete e, keep d; sha256 prefix 2803cbeb0deb51bf). Payload model: GEN (unigram, section, line position, copy and one-edit copy of the last 20 tokens) vs MSG (GEN + page recurrence + payload bigram) vs MSGSH (bigram trained on shuffled payloads). Controls: 5 generators fitted to the Voynich (WSHUF, MK2, JUNC, SC10, SELFCIT); Italian herbal, Latin Isidore and German through a payload code plus the same planted surface machinery (merge and verbose codes), the herbal also as a word-order-free list, and the generators fitted to each planted surface. Train on even leaves, test on odd leaves; ZL3b and IT2a | Planted texts: extraction returns the real words (purity 0.96-1.00) and restores their message (page recurrence 0.06-0.13 bits, sequence 0.06-1.1 bits; 80-95% of both is hidden on the raw surface). Voynich holdout: sequence excess 0.057 / 0.042 (Latin 0.06-0.10, German 0.15-0.20, junction generator 0.024, other generators 0); of the in-line gain, 77% is last glyph -> next word and only 0.016-0.020 bits is word identity (generators 0.001; Latin 0.07-0.11; German 0.13-0.16), 78-85% of it in 25 pairs (repeats, or/s/r + aiin, chedy~qokedy). Page recurrence 0.026 / 0.030 (below a 10%-copy generator at 0.043; all plants 0.055-0.125). Cross-page phrase recurrence 1.04x shuffles (plants 1.5-3.5x). Lexical-gap ratio G 1.04 (plants 0.52-0.73). Word arrows all from paragraph-first lines | **Not cracked. The assembled model fits, but its message layer carries no language-like message.** The Voynich's held-out structure sits in the surface machinery: edge pairing, the paragraph opening regime, adjacent repeats and space-split pieces. What survives stripping it is a 13-symbol, ~4-symbol-word, rigid-slot stream with section vocabulary, no topic recurrence, no recurring phrases and no lexical gaps |

| v78:V-78.1.V | Cycle verdict | | The doubled token is not a special doubling event. At the payload level the Voynich re-uses tokens inside a line at every short lag equally (no language-style avoidance of the neighbour, no doubling spike), and the second copy is re-spelled like any recurrence. The 'excess' over real systems (v75) is a concentrated vocabulary + line-level re-use + the absence of syntax's ban on neighbours. Implication if meaning is assumed: the unit written is not a word of running language (whose neighbours are constrained); it behaves like a value in a row (a cell, a syllable-like piece, a code item) drawn from a line's own small stock. Next (cycle 2): fit random mechanism mixtures to the doubles' full fingerprint with held-out leaves and calibrated control assignment, to bound how much of the doubling any special mechanism can carry |
